2) The "warm-start" and prefix-cache behavior: how latency evolves when new model variants or cold caches are exercised, and the recommended procedure for scaling replicas without violating tail-latency SLOs.

John, Nina —

Thanks for the clear ask. Below is a concise, engineer-facing description of our measurement methodology and the warm-start procedure we recommend for bake-off and operational runs. I'm attaching a compact PDF with runbook steps and a ZIP of sample histogram traces.

Summary (short):
- Measurement windows: collect steady-state samples over 30-minute sustained QPS and short spike windows of 60s and 5m.
- Metrics: per-request latency (end-to-end inference), model-internal token latency, KV cache hit-rate, GPU utilization, and tail percentiles (P50/P90/P99).
- Sequence buckets: short (<=16 tokens), mid (64-256), long (512-1024). Report per-bucket percentiles.
- Warm-start: use staged replica warming (prefix priming) + progressive traffic ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100% over configurable intervals) and soft-failover to warmed fallback variant.

Detailed methodology (engineer-facing):
1) Workload definition:
   - Steady-state profile: use your production QPS distribution or synthesize from provided histograms. For bake-off we often run at 25%, 50%, and 100% of your anticipated production QPS to validate linearity and cache effectiveness.
   - Spike scenarios: 60s spike at 3x peak QPS, and sustained 5m surge at 1.5x peak to expose autoscaling and queueing behavior.

2) Traffic generation:
   - Prefer replay of anonymized request logs where possible (preserving token-length and request-arrival distributions). If logs are not available, we provide a synthetic generator that respects token-length buckets, prompt complexity (short directives vs multi-turn), and user concurrency patterns.

3) Measurement and aggregation:
   - Collect per-request E2E latency with millisecond resolution at ingress and per-token timing inside the runtime.
   - Tag samples with model_version, endpoint_id, replica_id, cache_hit boolean, and warm_start boolean.
   - Use sliding windows (1m/5m/30m) and export histograms for P50/P90/P99. For P99 use max-likelihood estimation when sample counts are low.

4) Warm-start / prefix-cache ramping:
   - Cold replica behavior: first N requests incur KV-load penalties as caches populate; we quantify this as an approximate additive latency penalty per prefix token (empirically ~4-12ms/token depending on model and quantization).
   - Recommended warm-start procedure: provision new replicas out-of-band; send priming traffic consisting of sampled prefixes prioritized by frequency; then shift traffic with a progressive ramp described above.
   - Fallback policy: automatic fallback to warmed variants or a lower-cost cached variant if tail latency exceeds SLOs during rollout.

5) Acceptance criteria and artifacts:
   - For each sequence bucket report: P50/P90/P99, mean GPU utilization, cache hit-rate, and tail spike count (requests > SLO).
   - Attach trace samples (span-level with timestamps) and aggregated histograms for each run.

Attachments: redwood-latency-envelope-protocol.pdf (runbook, sample commands), warmstart-runbook-samples.zip (histogram CSVs + raw spans).

If helpful we can run an initial validation pass on a short sample of your traffic this week and share end-to-end plots. Markus and Lauren are looped for follow-up on run execution and any tweaks to the synthetic profiles.

Regards,

FYI — I looked over the proposed profiles. Two quick technical notes to prepare for the bake-off:

- For P99 under long sequences we should ensure we capture KV flush events and GPU context-switch overhead: recommend an additional 10-minute soak at target QPS with intermittent small IO noise to reproduce realistic cloud neighbors.
- For warm-start priming, include a high-frequency prefix set and a small set of low-frequency but long prefixes (to validate cold-cache tails). We'll seed those from our corpus; see attached manifest in the runbook.

I'll own instrumentation for span correlation and the example commands in the runbook. Lauren — can you confirm availability for a 30min test-run on Monday morning PST with EdgeScale?

-Markus
